speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you have noticed any recent fever, chills, or red streaks spreading from the area? Also, do you have any history of diabetes, recent insect bites, or travel to tropical regions?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Leishmaniasis (Cutaneous). Given the ulcerative lesion on the leg following an ant bite in a diabetic patient with Crohn's disease, this is highly suggestive of cutaneous leishmaniasis. I request images of the lesion to assess the ulcer's depth, borders, and any satellite lesions. REQUEST IMAGES: Leg_Ulcer_Photos
